title: Pilose antler peptide enhances diabetic fracture healing by modulating the CREB-Smad2/3-Runx2 signaling axis.
authors: Wang, Xin; Chen, Yibing; Cheng, Ziyang; Cao, Zhong; Cheng, ShuChao; Xin, Chao; Zhang, Jiayi; Zhang, Fengyi; Chen, Yaxin; Wang, Junyi; Li, Shufeng; Li, Yujie; Wang, Wenbo
one_liner_zh: 研究鹿茸肽通过CREB-Smad2/3-Runx2轴促进糖尿病骨折愈合，涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和分子对接，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD模拟方法，仅分子对接辅助，与TF-DNA课题关联弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cervi Cornu Pantotrichum, a cornerstone of traditional medicine, is prized for its bone-enhancing and metabolic-regulating effects. Pilose antler peptide (PAP), extracted from this remedy, offers a promising solution for diabetic fracture nonunion, a debilitating condition marked by hyperglycemia-impaired bone healing. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigates PAP's efficacy in accelerating diabetic fracture repair and delineates its molecular mechanisms, merging ethnopharmacological heritage with modern science. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diabetic fractures were induced in db/db mice, and PAP's effects were evaluated using micro-CT, histology, and osteogenic marker analysis. In vitro, high glucose-treated MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts mimicked diabetic conditions. Molecular mechanisms were probed via co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), fluorescence colocalization, molecular docking, and genetic modulation. RESULTS: PAP markedly improved fracture healing in diabetic mice, enhancing callus integrity, bone microarchitecture, and osteogenic marker levels. In osteoblasts, PAP counteracted high glucose-induced osteogenic suppression, boosting Runx2 expression while inhibiting CREB and Smad3 activation. Co-IP revealed PAP's disruption of the CREB-Smad2/3 complex, with colocalization showing diminished nuclear overlap of CREB and Smad2/3. Molecular docking identified PAP binding to CREB-Arg117 and Smad3-Glu246, supporting its inhibitory role. Genetic studies confirmed PAP's reversal of Smad2/3-mediated Runx2 suppression. CONCLUSION: PAP alleviates metabolic stress and promotes bone regeneration by targeting the CREB-Smad2/3-Runx2 axis. Rooted in ethnopharmacology, this multitarget peptide integrates traditional wisdom with cutting-edge molecular insights, presenting a novel therapeutic avenue for diabetic fracture management.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：鹿茸（Cervi Cornu Pantotrichum）作为传统医学的基石，因其增强骨骼和调节代谢的作用而备受珍视。从该药材中提取的鹿茸多肽（PAP）为糖尿病骨折不愈合提供了一种有前景的解决方案，这是一种以高血糖损害骨愈合为特征的衰弱性疾病。研究目的：本研究探讨PAP在加速糖尿病骨折修复中的疗效，并阐明其分子机制，将民族药理学遗产与现代科学相结合。材料与方法：在db/db小鼠中诱导糖尿病骨折，并通过micro-CT、组织学和成骨标志物分析评估PAP的效果。体外实验中，高糖处理的MC3T3-E1成骨细胞模拟糖尿病条件。通过免疫共沉淀 (co-immunoprecipitation, Co-IP)、荧光共定位、分子对接和遗传调控探讨分子机制。结果：PAP显著改善糖尿病小鼠的骨折愈合，增强骨痂完整性、骨微结构和成骨标志物水平。在成骨细胞中，PAP抵消了高糖诱导的成骨抑制，提升Runx2表达，同时抑制CREB和Smad3激活。Co-IP揭示PAP破坏CREB-Smad2/3复合物，共定位显示CREB和Smad2/3的核重叠减少。分子对接确定PAP与CREB-Arg117和Smad3-Glu246结合，支持其抑制作用。遗传研究证实PAP逆转Smad2/3介导的Runx2抑制。结论：PAP通过靶向CREB-Smad2/3-Runx2轴缓解代谢应激并促进骨再生。根植于民族药理学，这种多靶点多肽将传统智慧与前沿分子见解相结合，为糖尿病骨折管理提供了一种新的治疗途径。
